question.value: Can methanol 338.4 GHz outflow emission from modeled embedded low-mass protostars reproduce the observed extended methanol emission in a high-mass cluster, tracing the low-mass population?

evidence.quote: We here present a model of a forming cluster where methanol emission is assigned to every embedded low-mass protostar.

method.value: Sample positions, ages, IMF masses for 3000 stars; scale Class 0/I core masses

evidence.quote: The initial mass function (IMF) follows that defined in (cite: chabrier03) for young clusters and disk stars and is randomly sampled over the mass interval from 0.01–100 $M_\odot$
This relation works well with $R_0$=1 pc, $N_0$=300 and $\alpha=1/3$

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate methanol flux vs envelope mass

method.value: Correlate integrated intensity with envelope mass from JCMT maps; t test

evidence.quote: The proportionality is $S$ = (78$\pm$33) $M_{\rm env}$ Jy km s$^{-1}$ $M_\odot^{-1}$ where the uncertainty is 1$\sigma$.
at the 90% confidence level there is a direct proportionality between envelope mass and intensity

analysis_steps.goal: Assign outflow emission and make model image

method.value: Each lobe a 2D Gaussian of 2000 AU radius with flux scaled to envelope mass; Class I reduced by 10; convolve with beam

evidence.quote: scaling down the emission by a factor of ten for each Class I outflow. Finally, the map is convolved with the desired beam.
no radiative transfer is done explicitly, and that all emission is implicitly assumed to be optically thin

analysis_steps.goal: Compare model with ALMA radial profile

method.value: Radially average both images from cluster center, >3 sigma cut applied to both, primary beam accounted for

evidence.loc: 5.1 Comparison to ALMA observations of IRAS16547–4247
evidence.quote: both images are radially averaged from the center of the cluster including only fluxes $>$3$\sigma$
